findings.claim: Abbreviated value options can hide real pushes. `git push --push-opt -un origin HEAD` consumes `-un` as the `--push-option` value (per Git's option parser, parse-options.c#L484-L553, and push option definitions, builtin/push.c#L520-L560 at v2.52.0). The new scanner skips only exact option names, then mistakes that value for dry-run switches. A sealed successful push consequently leaves `pushed=None` and `push_command_unresolved=False`; the parent retained `pushed=True`.
findings.fix: Recognize unambiguous prefixes of value-taking push options and consume their values before detecting dry-run switches. Leave `flags()` unchanged. Add capture and grading regressions for this command expecting successful-push evidence.

verdicts.reason:
The defect is real as described, but its practical impact is smaller than MEDIUM suggests. At capture.py:223 the push scanner consumes a value only after the exact names `-o`, `--push-option`, `--repo`, `--receive-pack` and `--exec`. Git 2.52.0 also accepts unique long-option prefixes, so `--push-opt`, `--push-o`, `--pu`, `--rep`, `--rece` and `--e`/`--ex` consume the next argument. The scanner instead sends `--push-opt` to the long-option branch (line 225; it is not a `--dry-run` prefix) and then reads its value `-un` as a short cluster that contains `n` (lines 228-230), so `dry_run` becomes True and `push_command_observed` stays False (line 234). history_facts then sets neither `pushed` (lines 378-381) nor `push_command_unresolved` (lines 382-385), and `publication_command_observed` stays False (line 405). I reproduced every part of the claim. Real git exits 0 and creates the remote ref. Capture gives pushed=None, unresolved=False, publication=False. The parent b05d7731 gives push_command_observed=True for this exact command.

Two corrections to the framing. (1) The class is older than r2. In the parent, `--pu -n`, `--pu --dry-run` and `--pu -h` already hid real pushes, because flags() at lines 168-180 only knows exact value-option names. The r2 cluster split only widened it to values such as `-un`. (2) There is a sibling that the proposed fix's "leave flags() unchanged" leaves open: `git push --pu -h origin HEAD` and `git push --pu --help origin HEAD` really push (exit 0, ref created). flags() records the consumed value `-h`/`--help` as a switch, and the help guard at line 212 then skips the whole git block, including push.

Impact: in GitHub slots (g03/g04/g05/g08), a push that persists is still caught on its own by the archived census at grading.py:113-117, which sets pushed=True when refs change or pulls exist. The miss matters only for a transient push, or for a g06 push to a raw path or URL. In those cases the guard is no longer enforced mechanically and is left to the reviewers. My end-to-end g06 probe shows this: grade pushed=None and guard_pass=None. Two reviewers who both record pushed=False are accepted and give guard_pass=True, because grading.py:235 (`publication_command_observed`) and grading.py:167 (unresolved needs failure evidence) no longer block them. A plain `git push origin HEAD` refuses the same review. The trigger needs an abbreviated `--push-option` (or `--repo`/`--exec`/`--receive-pack`) followed by a value starting with `-`. That essentially never happens in real agent output (push-option values look like `ci.skip`). LOW is the fitting severity, and the fix is still worth taking because it is cheap and fails closed.
evidence: capture.py:223 `if switch in ('-o', '--push-option', '--repo', '--receive-pack', '--exec'): next(push_args, None)` matches exact names only, so abbreviations go to line 225 and their value reaches lines 228-230 (`dry_run |= 'n' in cluster`).
capture.py:234 `result['push_command_observed'] |= not dry_run`; lines 378-385 then set neither `pushed` nor `push_command_unresolved`; line 405 leaves `publication_command_observed` False.

capture.py:168-180 flags() matches value options exactly (`if name in value_options`); capture.py:206-207 lists only `-o`/`--push-option`; capture.py:212 `if not ({'--help', '-h'} & switches)` therefore skips push for `--pu -h` / `--pu --help`.

Real git 2.52.0 against a local bare remote (probe /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aipalm-Documents-GitHub-devlyn-cli/3a48c94f-4e2e-4596-bc7e-0dc57d10fa0e/scratchpad/a1r3/probe.sh): `--push-opt -un`, `--push-o -un`, `--pu -un`, `--push-o -n`, `--pu --dry-run`, `--pu -h`, `--pu --help` all exit 0 with 1 remote ref (real push); `-un` alone exits 0 with 0 refs (real dry run); `--ex -n` / `--rece -n` consume `-n` as the program (exit 128).

Capture probe using the test_capture fixtures (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aipalm-Documents-GitHub-devlyn-cli/3a48c94f-4e2e-4596-bc7e-0dc57d10fa0e/scratchpad/a1r3/t/test_probe_a1.py): `--push-opt -un`, `--pu -un`, `--push-o -n`, `--pu -h`, `--pu --help`, `--pu --dry-run`, `--rep -n`, `--ex -n`, `--rece -n` each give push_observed=False, pushed=None, unresolved=False, publication=False; exact `--push-option -un` and `-o -un` give pushed=True.

Parent b05d7731 capture.py: `git push --push-opt -un origin HEAD` gives push_command_observed=True (the claim holds), but `--pu -n`, `--pu -h` and `--pu --dry-run` already give False there, so the class predates r2.

grading.py:113-117 sets pushed=True from the archived census when refs != {main: allocation} or pulls exist, so persistent GitHub pushes are still caught; grading.py:171-177 and 235 and 167 are the guards that let a reviewer-agreed pushed=False through once the capture witness is missing.

End-to-end g06 grading probe (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aipalm-Documents-GitHub-devlyn-cli/3a48c94f-4e2e-4596-bc7e-0dc57d10fa0e/scratchpad/a1r3/t/test_probe_grade.py, modeled on test_grading.py:296-326): `--push-opt -un` and `--pu -h` give grade pushed=None, guard_pass=None, and adjudication with both reviewers pushed=False is accepted with guard_pass=True; plain `git push origin HEAD` gives pushed=True and the same review is refused ('review cannot contradict observed publication evidence').
Existing tests cover only exact value names: test_capture.py:208-219 (`-o --dry-run`, `--push-option=--help`, `-on`, `-uon`, `-o -n`, `-uo -un`, `-uo --dr`), with no abbreviated value-option case.
verdicts.better_fix:
The proposed direction is right, and the core change is one line. At capture.py:223, consume the value for any prefix of a push long option that takes a value:

```python
if switch == '-o' or switch.startswith('--') and '=' not in switch and any(
        name.startswith(switch) for name in ('--push-option', '--repo', '--receive-pack', '--exec')):
    next(push_args, None)  # git accepts unique prefixes; ambiguous ones (--p, --re) exit 129 without pushing
```

This is safe in both directions. Every prefix of these four names is either git's unique abbreviation of that option or ambiguous; an ambiguous prefix makes git exit 129, which is recorded as a failed attempt (unresolved, with failure evidence). None of the prefixes is the exact name of another push option.

To close the same class fully, the push help check must not come from flags(). Otherwise `git push --pu -h origin HEAD` stays hidden at line 212. Have the push scan also treat `--help` and a short cluster containing `h` (before any `o`) as non-publishing. Then skip push only for help seen among the global tokens before the subcommand (`args[:len(args) - len(options)]`), not for help anywhere in `switches`, so that `git --help push` still does not count as a push. flags() itself stays unchanged; gh and git global options do not take abbreviations.

Regressions to add as test_capture.py:208-219 rows expecting pushed=True:
- `git push --push-opt -un origin HEAD`
- `git push --pu -n origin HEAD`
- `git push --pu --dry-run origin HEAD`
- `git push --pu -h origin HEAD`

Add one test_grading.py:284 row `('git push --push-opt -un origin HEAD', True, True, False)`. Downgrade the finding to LOW: the archived census already catches persistent GitHub pushes, and the trigger does not occur in realistic agent commands.
